title: Counseling owed when the offer is accepted, and the statute on a declined offer
rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 94C, § 21A provides that if an offer to provide counseling is accepted, the pharmacist shall counsel the person presenting the prescription to the extent the pharmacist deems appropriate. Such counseling may include, but not be limited to: (1) the name and description of the medication; (2) the dosage form, dosage, route of administration and duration of drug therapy; (3) special instructions and precautions for preparation, administration and use by the patient; (4) common adverse or severe side effects or interactions and therapeutic contraindications that may be encountered, including their avoidance and the action required if they occur; (5) techniques for self-monitoring drug therapy; (6) proper storage; (7) prescription refill information; and (8) action to be taken in the event of a missed dose. The next paragraph provides that nothing in this section shall be construed to require a pharmacist to provide counseling if the person presenting the prescription declines to accept such offer for counseling. That disclaimer is stated of this section, that is, of M.G.L. c. 94C, § 21A.
exam_relevance: Supplies the statutory answer to the commonest Massachusetts counseling fact pattern, a new prescription on which the offer is made and declined, and gives the statute's own counseling-content menu, which differs in wording from the regulatory menu in 247 CMR 9.18(5).

authority.name: Massachusetts General Laws
authority.section: M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21A, fifth and sixth paragraphs

exceptions: Nothing in M.G.L. c. 94C, § 21A shall be construed to require a pharmacist to provide counseling if the person presenting the prescription declines to accept the offer for counseling.
common_confusions: The statutory duty to counsel is conditioned on the offer being accepted; the extent of the counseling is then what the pharmacist deems appropriate.
The eight-item statutory list is introduced by 'may include, but not be limited to', so it is neither a required script nor a closed set.
The declination disclaimer is stated of M.G.L. c. 94C, § 21A itself; it is not worded as a disclaimer of any other counseling provision.
verification_notes: Read in the current text of M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 21A on malegislature.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed.
